recipes.name: Sweet Potato Casserole Dessert
ingredients_raw: 4.5 cups cooked and mashed sweet potatoes

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Mix mashed sweet potatoes, sugar, 1/2 cup melted butter, milk, eggs, and vanilla extract together in a large bowl; spread into the prepared baking dish.
Mix brown sugar and flour together in a small bowl; cut in 1/3 cup butter until mixture is crumbly, then stir in pecans. Sprinkle streusel mixture over sweet potatoes.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Potato Casserole Dessert
raw_recipe.description: This fluffy sweet potato casserole dessert with its crunchy pecan streusel topping makes a fantastic, crowd-pleasing dish for the holidays.

review.reviewBody: I made this for Easter and it was a hit with the family. I did adapt the recipe according to what others have suggested. I used two 29-oz cans of cut sweet potatoes instead of cooking my own. I substitued evaporated milk for the regular milk and I think it made it more creamy. I used dark brown sugar for the white sugar and I cut that back to 3/4 cup since others said 1 cup made it too sweet. I upped the vanilla to 1 tsp. I was going to add 1 tsp. cinnamon, 1/2 tsp. nutmeg and 1/2 tsp. salt to the mixture but I forgot until it was too late. But I did manage to get a sprinkling of cinnamon on the casserole before I put the topping on. I made a double batch of the topping and baked it all in a 9 x 13 pan. It was fantastic!

Family raved. For optimal sweet potato flavor, I cut them in half lengthwise, brushed the inside with olive oil and sprinkled with nutmeg allspice and cinnamon, then baked them face down on a cookie sheet in the oven at 350 degrees for 45 minutes. Able to peel the skin right off with you hand by that point, and the sweet potato’s are juicy and flavorful. Be sure to mix well with and electric mixer

My favorite sweet potato casserole recipe yet! I changed it slightly based on reviews. My changes: 1/3 cup of white sugar, 1/4 cup maple syrup, no milk, 1 egg, no vanilla, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, cook the pecan topping on the stove adding 1/4 cup of milk to all other topping ingredients, then pour over sweet potato mixture. Bake for 25 minutes at 350. Delicious

I apologize in advance for all the modifications I made to the recipe. Some modifications I did in my attempt to make this comfort food slightly “healthier”, if that word can even be used in such a dish. 😊 I followed some of the measurements but the following I modified. For the filling, I used ½ cup of light brown sugar, 2 tablespoons of heavy cream instead of milk, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, ½ teaspoon of ground cinnamon, and ¼ teaspoon salt. For the topping, I used ½ cup of butter, ¾ cup of light brown sugar, ¾ cup of pecans, and a sprinkle of marshmallows. The casserole dish I used was able to hold all of the filling but only some of the topping. I saved the remaining topping for another day. I probably used about 2 cups of the topping, but in all honesty, I did not measure it.

This was delicious! I used two large cans of drained sweet potatoes, then cut the sugar in half since the potatoes were canned in heavy syrup. I used brown sugar instead of of white sugar and added 1 tsp. of vanilla and 1/2 tsp. of cinnamon.

I've made this every Thanksgiving for at least the past 10 years. I boil sweet potatoes whole, then slide the skins off & mash. I double the topping because we love it so much. We have subbed walnuts based on price/availability.

I made this for Christmas and everyone loved it! I did make the sweet potatoes the night before and used 1/2 the sugar. Then made the topping before I put in oven, and what a hit this was! Will definitely make again!

I've made this recipe many, many times during Thanksgiving and Christmas. My family never tires of it!
I don't like the taste of raisins after they are cooked, so I have experimented with a couple of variations that I would like to share. Everyone at my holiday table usually ask for second helpings!
I drain a small can of crushed pineapple and squeeze it out in paper towels to remove all the juice I can, then add a tablespoon or 2 to the potato mixture, I also add a little flaked coconut and dried cranberries, (all in amounts to your liking), and bake as directed. Really good!
I have also made the recipe, partially cook it without the topping, then fill small fillo pastry cups, topped with streusel topping and bake until pastry cups start to brown.
They make great bite sized "casseroles" when the menu is lighter!

I haven't seen this tweak in the reviews so I thought I would add it because there are many people who have dietary challenges. I take this (by request) to our annual church Thanksgiving dinner, but one of the members has a severe nut allergy, so no pecans. I got creative and added shredded coconut for the topping instead, thinking it would be the volume I needed but have very little flavor. I was so wrong. The coconut is a perfect substitute and for my nut-loving family, I just add the coconut to the topping ingredients so we have both pecans and coconut. No other changes, a delightful recipe.

Made this yesterday. Sorry, but I too made some very slight adjustments. Used ½ and ½ instead of milk, and ½ cup packed brown sugar instead of 1 cup white sugar. I have never made sweet potato casserole before but this recipe looked wonderful so I tried it. I brought it to a potluck dinner and everyone raved about it. Even the two women from "down south" gave it high praises and one had more instead of dessert! Thank you for a great recipe that I will make over and over and over again! Lunch lady Elaine

I make it every holiday and I've even convinced those that don't like sweet potatoes to try it anyway and they love it as much as those of us that love sweet potatoes! I use a bit of pumpkin pie seasoning in the potatoes and instead of pecans i use pistachios ground/chopped up on top! Lovely and heavenly!
Recipe was pretty simple to make. I added nutmeg, cinnamon, and light brown sugar to sweet potato mix for additional flavor. I also added some marshmallows to the center topping for flavor.
Easy very good was liked by everyone
Baked in a toaster oven for an hour.
Delicious! Due to crowd control, I put miniature marshmallows on top of half, and the pecan pieces on the other half of the top.
My family said it was the best I’ve made. I did use homemade bourbon vanilla extract, but made it per the recipe.
Added frosted cornflakes in with the topping for extra crunch
